summary: Guidance: isolate keepalive/telemetry heartbeats from ingest burst pool to prevent early 429s
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports repeated 429 throttles during scheduled bulk ingest windows despite apparent spare burst credits. Impact: their nightly import jobs (multipart uploads + streaming websocket sessions) see ~10-15% failure rate from 429s, causing retries and delays to downstream pipeline. Environment: enterprise tenant on dedicated pool (prod-us-west), using a multiplexed upload orchestrator + long-lived SSE connections for progress telemetry.

Observed behavior: 429s begin shortly after the import job starts and are correlated with a burst of short keepalive/telemetry messages from worker agents. The console shows burst pool credits depleting even when the main payload token accounting is within limits. Customer requests guidance on separating heartbeat/telemetry traffic from ingest burst accounting and asks whether Redwood supports a dedicated burst lane or an exclusion rule for internal probes.

Expected behavior: keepalive/telemetry heartbeat traffic should be either exempted from the user-facing burst pool or charged to a different, configurable background pool to avoid early occupancy and unexpected 429s for high-priority ingest jobs.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Start a scheduled bulk import with 50 parallel uploader workers against the customer's dedicated pool.
2) Each worker opens a streaming websocket or SSE session for progress telemetry and sends a 1kB keepalive ping every 5-10s.
3) Observe rate-limit telemetry and console token-burst counters for the tenant.
4) Notice 429s appear on upload requests within 60-120s of job start and burst credits in console drop rapidly despite low payload throughput.

Notes: reproduces reliably when worker count >= 30 and keepalive interval <= 10s; does not reproduce with keepalive disabled or set to > 45s.

comments: 2026-03-10 09:17 - Customer (NimbleForms): We're seeing 429s right after our import jobs start. The console shows burst credit zeroing out despite our main throughput being well below limits. Can you explain why keepalives are drawing from the same burst budget?

2026-03-10 09:35 - Support (Aisha Patel): Thanks for the report — opening ticket and investigating. Please confirm approximate keepalive interval and number of concurrent workers. Also share a recent console snapshot if possible.
2026-03-10 10:02 - Customer: Worker count ~50, keepalive 8s, using SSE for telemetry. Attaching console image (already uploaded to support portal).

2026-03-10 16:10 - SRE (Liam OConnor): Initial hypothesis: keepalive/telemetry pings are currently charged to the same token/burst pool as upload requests. For many small pings at high concurrency, the token-bucket accounting on the ingress edge can be exhausted before larger payload tokens are fully considered due to ordering. Investigating whether health checks and proxied pings are being filtered before rate accounting.

2026-03-11 08:24 - Eng (Priya Shah): Reproduced locally with worker simulator. Confirmed that edge-proxy counts every inbound message (including SSE keepalive) against tenant burst window. Filing small change to allow route-level exemption rules or separate background pool config.

2026-03-12 13:40 - Support (Aisha Patel): Shared mitigation steps: increase keepalive interval to >=30s, add jitter, and temporarily reduce concurrent workers to avoid synchronized pings. Customer testing now.
2026-03-12 16:05 - Customer: Tested recommended changes (keepalive 45s + jitter) and 429 rate dropped to <1%. Looking for permanent config change and docs on recommended patterns.

2026-03-12 18:22 - Eng (Liam OConnor): Preparing rollout for a config flag to exclude well-known internal telemetry routes (/v1/telemetry/keepalive, /health/ping) from burst accounting and to support a dedicated background burst pool. Will target canary in prod-us-west next week.
investigation_notes: Edge token-bucket is route-agnostic by default; all inbound requests are normalized and tokenized before route weighting applies — small messages (keepalive) can create many low-cost token events that accumulate quickly in short windows.

Observed ordering effect: many small events can drive pre_count->0 before larger upload requests are processed by backend convolution, resulting in 429s on high-cost payload requests even though sustained budget is available.
Health checks and SSE pings are not currently filtered by default in the dedicated pool config. This is by design to ensure accounting but harms high-concurrency ingest patterns.
Short-term mitigation verified: changing keepalive interval to 30-60s with jitter prevents synchronized token consumption and removes wave pattern of 429s.

Long-term fix options: 1) Exempt identified internal telemetry routes from tenant burst accounting. 2) Add configurable secondary 'background' token pool for probes/telemetry. 3) Provide console flag to split burst credits by route-class (interactive vs background).
resolution: Partial workaround applied; long-term config work approved
resolution_notes: Applied customer-facing mitigation guidance: increase keepalive interval and add jitter. Customer reports >99% success rate for import after change.
Eng approved change: add route-level exclusion and background pool feature. PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/rate-limiter/pull/432 (feature branch).
Canary plan: enable exclusion for NimbleForms in prod-us-west for next maintenance window; monitor burst_pool metrics and 429 rate for 48h. If stable, promote to platform config with docs update.

Follow-ups: update developer docs with best practices for multiplexed uploader + telemetry (recommended keepalive >=30s, jitter, client backoff). Create KB article for Dedicated customers: 'Separating telemetry/healthchecks from burst accounting.'
